text.p: These are the leading stories in the Moroccan press on Sunday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Higher education minister meets university officials and students in Casablanca and says ministry to investigate problems of overcrowding in some faculties and problems of transport for students.
- Islamic Conference Organisation secretary-general Azzedine Laraki, during visit in Casablanca, says trade between member states should receive particular attention in years ahead.
- Twenty-eight percent of Moroccan unemployed have a degree, 40 percent of children aged eight to 13 do not attend school, says Istiqlal executive committee member.
- New law faculty will be created at Settat to diminish overcrowding in existing faculty, and 150 more buses will reinforce university transport in two months.
- Morocco and Japan preparing technical cooperation project to develop fish stocks, particularly sardines, in Moroccan waters.
